headline: FREEPORT OKS $4.5B BAGDAD BET — Arizona Copper to Double Output to 400M+ Lbs/Yr by Mid-2030
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan approved a $4.5 billion expansion of its Bagdad mine in Arizona on November 4, targeting roughly 225 million additional pounds per year that would take total Bagdad copper output above 400 million pounds annually — alongside a 12 million pound per year increase in molybdenum — with first production targeted for mid-2030 based on $4.00/lb copper economics. The board decision came alongside Q3 earnings in which Freeport simultaneously trimmed its 2026-27 copper sales guidance by 2–2.5% and raised 2027 capex to $5.2 billion, lifting total 2027 capital commitments well above $9 billion.

headline: CENTERRA + BHP BOTH BACK MUNDORO — C$4M Stake + 5 Drill-Ready Porphyry Targets in Serbia's Timok; Two Majors Endorse One TSXV Junior
snippet: Mundoro Capital (TSXV: MUN) on November 6 simultaneously reported 2026 Timok exploration results — 100% ownership of eight licenses in Serbia's Timok Magmatic Complex with five drill-ready porphyry copper-gold targets — and announced Centerra Gold's C$4.08 million strategic investment for a 9.9% stake via private placement at C$0.33/share. BHP has separately funded C$18.9 million across four drill programs at Mundoro's Borsko and Central Timok properties since 2023, making Centerra the second major miner to put money behind the same TSXV junior hunting tier-1 copper-gold porphyry deposits in Europe.

headline: UR-ENERGY CEO: WYOMING URANIUM IS JUST GETTING STARTED — Shirley Basin Restart + Lost Creek Hub Eyes 4.2M Lbs; Acquisitions Targeted
snippet: In a Northern Miner interview published November 6, Ur-Energy's CEO discussed the company's growing Wyoming uranium platform following the successful restart of Shirley Basin — the first uranium production at that site since 1992 — and outlined expansion plans beyond the current 4.2 million pound per year combined licensed capacity at Lost Creek and Shirley Basin through drilling, acquisitions, and toll-processing. Shirley Basin operates as a satellite producing uranium-bearing resin trucked to the Lost Creek hub for final processing; a 120-hole step-out program at Lost Creek South was recently approved, and the CEO said acquisitions of additional Wyoming ISR assets are under active evaluation as spot uranium approaches US$92 per pound.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM CARBONATE 40% — $12,000/t Three-Month Target on Battery Demand Slowdown
snippet: Citigroup cut its three-month lithium carbonate price target by 40% to US$12,000 per tonne from US$20,000, and reduced hydroxide to US$12,000 from US$17,000 and spodumene to US$1,200 from US$2,000, citing a worsening battery demand growth outlook driven by slowing EV adoption rates, rising trade uncertainty, and broader macroeconomic headwinds. The bearish reassessment from one of the most-watched sell-side lithium analysts reinforces the discount at which TSX-V and ASX lithium developers trade relative to their resource-based valuations, and raises the bar further for junior lithium projects to attract institutional capital.

headline: DENISON'S PHOENIX ISR MINE 24% BUILT — $161M Spent; Freeze Wells Drilling, Process Plant Concrete Poured Before Winter
snippet: Denison Mines reported Q3 2026 results on November 4 showing the Phoenix ISR uranium mine 24% complete after one full quarter of full-scale construction — with year-to-date capital expenditure of $161.1 million against a full-year 2026 budget of $278.6 million. Concrete work for the process plant building was substantially complete before Saskatchewan winter arrived, freeze well drilling has commenced, and new early-stage Phoenix North mineralization has been identified within the project footprint; first production remains on track for the second half of 2028, which would make Phoenix Canada's first new uranium mine in a generation.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH PAUSE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — Four Days Out: What It Means for USAR, MP Materials, and Western Miners
snippet: With China's October 2025 rare earth export control suspension expiring November 10 — four days away — Motley Fool's analysis flags USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) as the key North American stocks on watch for the binary outcome: Beijing reinstates restrictions (bullish for Western producers) or extends the pause to January 2027 under the broader US-China arrangement currently debated by Treasury. China controls roughly 70% of global rare earth extraction and 90% of downstream processing, meaning any tightening hits defence and EV supply chains with no short-term substitute.

headline: GOLD EQUITIES LAGGING GOLD POST-ELECTION — VanEck's Casanova: Disconnect at $4,050 Spot 'Won't Last'
snippet: VanEck portfolio manager Imaru Casanova — who runs the Gold Miners ETF (GDX) — argues that the persistent underperformance of gold equities versus bullion following the Democratic midterm sweep is a temporary post-election dislocation rather than a structural re-rating lower. Casanova highlights that major gold producers are running at record free cash flow margins with spot above $4,050 and all-in sustaining costs averaging below $1,900/oz, and that the equity-to-metal discount historically closes within two to three quarters after a sharp divergence — representing an opportunity for investors comfortable holding through near-term macro uncertainty.

headline: GOLD FALLS TO $4,039 ON HOT JOBS REPORT — Dollar Surges 0.7%, December Rate Cut Odds Fade After October Payrolls Beat
snippet: Gold slid to approximately US$4,039 per ounce on November 6 as a stronger-than-expected October payrolls report lifted the US dollar index roughly 0.7% and prompted futures markets to pare December Federal Reserve rate cut probabilities — adding a second bearish catalyst to the profit-taking from gold's post-election surge to $4,136 earlier in the week. The result creates a near-term headwind for the gold and silver bull case, though analysts note that central bank buying reportedly hit a 2026 high this week and the structural demand story from emerging market central banks remains intact as a floor.
